title: The Next Medium: Why Real-Time Interactive Video Changes Everything — Ahmed Ahres, Reactor
talk_summary: A go-to-market talk about Reactor's platform for real-time interactive video/world models, arguing that real-time generation turns video from a passive 'slot machine' into programmable, controllable media. It is almost entirely about a different product domain (GPU video inference, streaming, global latency) with no engineering practices for agent orchestration.

takeaways.technique: Separate real-time serving infra from batch job infra
takeaways.what_they_do: They argue batch inference architecture (request -> cloud job -> file) cannot be reused for real-time serving, which needs streaming, persistent live sessions with memory, and geo-routed GPUs for sub-100ms latency.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you cannot just take what works for batch inference and apply to real-time inference

takeaways.what_they_do: They admit evaluation of real-time generative models is unsolved and currently done by looking at output and human judgment, even at DeepMind.
takeaways.evidence_quote: evaluation for these real-time models is an unsolved problem. So today it's literally just look at it and human judgment
